title: "menuSelect" is not working in IE
body: Hi! I have a documentation issue on InstantSearch.js. I could not find what I was looking for on the page "[menuSelect](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/v2/widgets/menuSelect.html

comments.body:
`menuSelect` is expected to work in IE, could you share a bug reproduction?

Note that the code snippets use the ES6 syntax, which might break on that browser. In this case, you may want to replace `const`s with `var`s.

Thank you for your reply.
Please check follwoing sandbox.
https://codesandbox.io/s/v81oyyw657
I can't show menuselect widget on IE with url https://v81oyyw657.codesandbox.io/

CodeSandbox is not IE-compatible. You can see the `menuSelect` widget working on IE in the [storybook](https://instantsearchjs.netlify.com/stories/?selectedKind=MenuSelect&selectedStory=default&full=0&addons=1&stories=1&panelRight=0&addonPanel=storybook%2Factions%2Factions-panel).

Closing this issue. Feel free to open other ones if you need anything!
As I said in my first answer, you need to replace the `const`s to `var`s. You might also need to remove any trailing coma if you want to support old versions of IE.

Thanks a million Francoi! I have tried as you tought, but still not working. please check my following file and let me know what is wrong. ais-ecommerce-demo-app

InstantSearch.js e-commerce demo

Brands

I wrote above code in one file "index.html" and run it with Chrome and IE. In Chrome, it works well, but in IE it didn't work. Please kindly check my code and give me your advice. Thank you.
Which version of IE are you using? What error is thrown?

IE is version 11.523.17134.0
And menuselect is not displayed on IE.
Thank you.

After checking the implementation, we use [`Array.prototype.find`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/find), which is not supported by IE by default.

For the widget to work in IE, you can add polyfills to your page:

```html
<script src="https://polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js?features=default,Array.prototype.find,Array.prototype.includes"></script>
```

We'll make sure to document that on the new documentation website.

Great!
Working well now.
